title: Deep init emits compact automation manifest
query: A new Farplane project is being initialized with a PM heartbeat, daily PM plan, weekly PM plan, and optional ticket drainer. What should the generated farplane/automations.md contain versus leave to skills?
reference_points: Keeps schedules, target threads, gates, grouped jobs, freshness, reports, and local overrides in farplane/automations.md
Uses a compact job_catalog or equivalent skill-preset references instead of duplicating every job's reads/writes/output runbook
Names separate skill-owned presets such as pm-heartbeat.bandit, daily-pm-plan.operating_plan, weekly-pm-plan.strategy, and ticket-drainer.daily
Includes a compile rule requiring live Codex prompts to inline enough ordered steps to run safely
Does not collapse the cadence skills into one router or leave live automation prompts as vague 'read the manifest and decide' instructions

title: Deep init ticket drainer uses parent-spawned child threads
query: The generated daily ticket drainer is kept as a separate execution selector that may be invoked by the daily plan or short heartbeat. What thread contract should the template encode?
reference_points: Ticket drainer remains a separate skill rather than being hidden inside a PM router
Parent cadence names or creates the child thread using a ticket-based title template
Child prompt includes project root, parent cadence id, ticket path, context refs, expected outputs, side-effect gates, and lineage writeback
The template records child thread id or handoff blocker in reports and run ledger
It does not ask the child worker to rename itself
